visual.summary: Visitors' camp level 3: the same as level 2 plus a few flowers and grass.
problems: The bright blue and cyan wool tents clash with the timber-and-stone style: use white, brown or green wool with spruce poles, or striped (two colours) canvas.
The tents are solid stepped wool lumps: give them an open front with a fence pole and a bedroll or carpet inside.
Level 3 barely differs from level 2 (a few flowers): give it its own feature (a market stall with an awning, a horse post with a cart, a washing line).

visual.summary: Level 3 adds a red and white striped market awning over the crates, which clearly sets it apart from L2. Tents still look stepped.
problems: The tents still read as green wool staircases, and the white stripes show as scattered spots on the steps. Make each tent a clean A-frame: one colour per slope, a white or brown trim row only along the bottom edge, a fence or log ridge pole sticking out at front and back, and a fence pole at each front corner

The layout is scattered: tents, stall and crates sit at odd angles round the fire with gaps. Put the two tents facing the fire on either side, the stall and woodpile at the back, and a gravel or coarse dirt patch under the fire so it reads as one camp
Red awning, red banners and green tents together are loud: a brown or white awning would sit better
